key_highlights: ASX slides as oil spike from Saudi/Hormuz tensions fuels RBA rate-hike bets; big four banks (CBA, ANZ, NAB, WBC) fall
Iron ore in structural decline – BHP.AX under existential pressure, FMG.AX and RIO.AX exposed
RBA deputy governor signals inflation still too high, raising probability of further tightening
Home buyer sentiment collapses; property industry faces 'GFC moment' – REITs and construction names at risk
Gold mining sector active: Forrestania, Kaiser, Manhattan, Larvotto, Aureka all report positive discoveries/deals
Santos (STO.AX) gas cartel dynamics shifting; Hormuz escalation threatens LNG supply chains
Qantas (QAN.AX) $35M worker payout and jet incident weigh on sentiment
Living standards collapse narrative: second jobs, mortgage stress, public sector boom masking decline

sectors.trend: Iron ore in structural downturn; BHP.AX, FMG.AX, RIO.AX under severe pressure. Gold miners (FOR.AX, KAL.AX, MNG.AX, LRV.AX, ARK.AX) see positive catalysts from new discoveries and M&A.
sectors.implications: Rotate out of iron ore/coal exposure; gold miners offer relative strength and inflation hedge. Diversify into uranium (INF.AX) and antimony/tungsten (LRV.AX).

sectors.trend: Big four (CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX) fall on rate-hike fears and property credit risk. Housing downturn threatens NPLs. ATO vs Big Tech tax fight adds policy uncertainty.
sectors.implications: Short-term headwind from rate expectations; medium-term credit risk from property GFC moment. Monitor NPL trends and RBA commentary closely.

sectors.trend: Oil spike from Saudi attacks and Hormuz escalation lifts energy names. Santos (STO.AX) gas cartel dynamics shifting. LNG supply chain at geopolitical risk.
sectors.implications: Short-term tailwind for oil/LNG producers (WDS.AX, WLE.AX, STO.AX). Hormuz risk is a double-edged sword – bullish energy, bearish global growth.

sectors.trend: Home buyer sentiment collapses; property faces GFC moment. Mortgage stress driving second jobs. REITs (GPW.AX, SPG.AX, ICPL.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure.
sectors.implications: Defensive consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) may outperform. REITs under pressure from rate sensitivity and demand weakness.

sectors.trend: CSL.AX relatively insulated. US tech (AMD, MU, ADBE) shows AI/HBM demand strength but elevated expectations create vulnerability. ATO tax fight targets Big Tech in Australia.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains a defensive anchor. Australian tech exposure limited; monitor ATO enforcement impact on foreign tech revenue.

opportunities.rationale: Multiple positive discoveries (Forrestania, Kaiser, Manhattan, Larvotto) plus geopolitical risk premium support gold

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical overweight energy on oil spike and Hormuz risk
opportunities.rationale: Saudi attacks and Hormuz escalation create supply risk premium; Santos gas dynamics shifting

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive tilt to CSL.AX and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: Insulated from commodity and rate cycles; essential demand resilient in living standards squeeze

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or exit iron ore exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Structural decline confirmed; BHP existential question; no near-term catalyst for reversal
Housing GFC moment, collapsing buyer sentiment, rate-hike risk create downside

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim big four bank exposure pending NPL data
defensive_moves.rationale: Rate-hike fears plus property credit risk create dual headwind
$35M payout, jet incident, and operational issues create overhang

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX under pressure from oil-driven rate-hike fears, iron ore weakness, and property stress. Expect continued bank and materials underperformance. Gold and energy provide relative strength. RBA commentary is the key swing factor.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautious. Structural iron ore decline and housing correction weigh on growth. Gold mining and energy offer diversification. Living standards squeeze may force policy response. ATO enforcement on Big Tech adds revenue but creates friction. 6-12 month path depends on RBA pivot timing and commodity stabilisation.
